name: Bounded Common-Section Composition
statement: For common-section pieces $A_1,\ldots,A_m$ over $D$, let $X_I=\bigcup_{i\in I}A_i$, $X_\emptyset=D$, $N=|D|$, and $r_i=\sigma(A_i;D)$. Then $\sigma(X;D)=\max_i r_i$, $\sigma(X)=\min_{|I|\leq N}\max(\{\sigma(X_I)\}\cup\{r_i:i\notin I\})$, and $\sigma(X)=\max_{|J|\leq N+1}\sigma(X_J)$. For $m$ disjoint private copies of one piece $A$, $\sigma(X^{(m)})=\sigma(A;D)$ whenever $m\geq|D|+1$.
proof: Putting $D$ first and appending optimal local outside orders proves the relative formula, because every cross-piece disagreement contains the gate disagreement. For an arbitrary global order, mark for each $d\in D$ the piece containing the first word projected to $d$; at most $|D|$ pieces are marked. In every unmarked piece, moving all of $D$ first preserves the width: a newly minimal gate support is bounded using the earlier marked word over the same projection. This proves the minimization formula. A threshold argument then shows that some subunion of at most $|D|+1$ pieces realizes the full width. Identical copies give the final identity.
comments: Every threshold failure is witnessed by at most $|D|+1$ pieces of the displayed decomposition; this does not bound the cardinality of an intrinsic forbidden pc-minor. The gluing preserves ampleness and the partial-cube property when all pieces have it.
